dedupe_keys.name: who global status report on road safety 2023 country and territory data

description: The Global status report on road safety 2023 is the fifth such report led by the World Health Organization. It details road traffic deaths and progress on laws, strategies and actions between 2010 and 2021, and sets a baseline for the UN Decade of Action for Road Safety 2021-2030; annual deaths fell slightly to 1.19 million. Coverage: countries and territories that took part in the GSRRS 2023 survey, answered by government-designated national data focal points between September 2022 and August 2023. Format and access: the report, country and territory profiles, the survey questionnaire and an Excel file of the profile data, which also holds WHO's 2023 update of fatality estimates for 2010 and 2016 onwards with confidence intervals and rates per 100,000 population; countries are keyed by ISO3 code. Licence and cost: free; the page states no licence. Caveats: the survey is one of several sources, and some countries did not take part; the Excel's second row holds text descriptions. The data give a comparative baseline of road-safety outcomes and policies for resilience and policy studies of road networks. It relates to the EU CARE database, iRAP and GB STATS19 in the catalogue.
